title: Unraveling the Emergence of Slow Dynamics in U(1) Lattice Gauge Theories
authors: Riccardo Andreoni, Zala Lenarčič, Zeno Bacciconi, Antonello Scardicchio, Marcello Dalmonte, Devendra Singh Bhakuni
abstract: The dynamics of gauge theories is of fundamental interest, with low-dimensional systems displaying a rich phenomenology beyond the rapid thermalization typical of QCD and non-Abelian theories. In particular, recent quantum simulation experiments have reported robust and unexpected signatures of slow relaxation in generic regimes and at large volumes in one-dimensional U(1) lattice gauge theories (LGTs), whose origin remains poorly understood. Here, we present a framework that provides a unified perspective on such slow dynamics and establishes a new route for exploring subdiffusive fractonic hydrodynamics in Rydberg experiments. The backbone of our theory is an exact analytical mapping from U(1) LGTs with a topological $θ$ angle to non-local kinetically constrained fermionic models with an emergent linear Stark potential. In the absence of the $θ$ term, this framework interprets the non-thermal dynamics reported in recent experiments as prethermal behavior arising from proximity to an integrable free-fermion model. For non-zero $θ$, the emergent Stark potential instead explains the freezing dynamics observed in other recent experiments. We argue that this correspondence could also lead to subdiffusive transport due to emergent conservation laws. We predict that these phenomena arise in a much broader class of models, and support this prediction with numerical simulations and proposals for future experiments.
summary: This work unifies the understanding of slow dynamics in U(1) Lattice Gauge Theories by mapping them onto constrained fermionic models. The authors show that non-thermal behavior can be explained either as prethermalization (no $\theta$ term) or freezing due to an emergent Stark potential ($\theta$ term). This suggests that subdiffusive transport is a generic feature arising from emergent conservation laws in these systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the poorly understood origin of slow, non-thermal dynamics (such as subdiffusion or freezing) observed in one-dimensional U(1) Lattice Gauge Theories (LGTs).
main_result: The authors establish an exact analytical mapping from U(1) LGTs to non-local kinetically constrained fermionic models, showing that non-thermal behavior arises from proximity to integrable models or emergent conservation laws.
method: The core method involves deriving a dual fermionic description by integrating out gauge degrees of freedom and analyzing the resulting Hamiltonian structure.
model_or_system: The system is the U(1) LGT, which is mapped to a fermionic model featuring an emergent linear Stark potential. The analysis is performed on 1D systems, drawing parallels to Rydberg atom arrays.
key_observables: Electric-field correlations, subsystem charge fluctuations, and the decay profile of spin transport ($	ilde{C}_s(x, t)$).
important_parameters: The topological $\theta$ angle, the constraint radius $R$, and the system size $L$.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes the existence of an exact analytical mapping between the gauge theory and the constrained fermionic model.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the mapping from the Rydberg Hamiltonian to the constrained Wannier-Stark model, and show the finite-size scaling of charge fluctuations ($O_d(t)$) for different constraint radii $R$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first introducing the physical problem (slow dynamics in LGTs), then presenting the exact mapping to the fermionic model, and finally analyzing the resulting dynamics using conservation laws and scaling arguments.
why_interesting: It provides a deep theoretical link between gauge field dynamics and fermionic models exhibiting non-equilibrium behavior, which is highly relevant for understanding quantum simulation results in Rydberg arrays.
